purpose: Independently recode the source-bound civilian-harm evidence after the first-coder source-independence coverage gap was filled, without exposing first-coder values or Pineland outputs.

second_coder_may_see: blind packet containing case, source identity, URL/archive reference, and source locator
second_coder_must_not_see: first-coder values, component choices, actor choices, admission decisions, or notes
Pineland predictions, residuals, model states, or historical diagnostic outputs
blindness.packet_rule: One blind item is one unique source locator. If the locator contains multiple admissible civilian-harm records, the second coder returns all of them.

agreement_unit: Source-locator record set, followed by matched record-level agreement within each locator.

prospective_matching.matching_rule: Use maximum-cardinality one-to-one matching within each source locator. Exact component and measure are required for a record match; date/geography must overlap rather than be invented into equality.
prospective_matching.actor_rule: Normalization is frozen here before second coding. It is applied only for agreement scoring and never changes source-native coding.

numeric_semantics.point: Exact source-native numeric agreement required when both coders record a point value.
numeric_semantics.lower_bound: Values agree if both preserve the same reported lower bound and neither invents an unsupported upper bound.
numeric_semantics.upper_bound: Values agree if both preserve the same reported upper bound and neither invents an unsupported lower bound.
numeric_semantics.range: Both reported lower and upper bounds must agree exactly.
numeric_semantics.qualitative_only: Agreement requires both coders to leave unsupported numeric fields blank.

gate_rule: All pre-adjudication thresholds must pass. Primary metrics are preserved even if later adjudication resolves disagreements; no post-hoc threshold relaxation or alternate primary metric is permitted.
after_second_coding: hash-lock completed second-coder output before reading first-coder values for comparison
adjudicate only after primary score is written
confirmatory historical harm use remains additionally blocked by model semantic/retention compatibility
